data.name: Thirza
data.gender_notes: Thirza is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Thirza means 'jasmine' or 'rose'. This beautiful and fragrant flower has been used as a symbol of love and devotion in various cultures and religious traditions. The name Thirza carries the meaning “Jasmine or rose” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Thirza usually hope their child will grow to embody jasmine or rose and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents love, beauty, and grace in the spiritual realm.
data.etymology: Thirza belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jasmine or rose.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thirza total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: תִּרְצָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תִּרְצָה (Thirza) – שְׁמוּעַ חָדָשׁ, 'שְׁמוּעַ בְּשִׁפְטֶיהָ' (1 Samuel 25:3). מְקוֹר נַחֲלָה (2 Chronicles 22:11). 'רְצוֹן' (Proverbs 19:22). 'אֱהָבָה' (1 Samuel 16:7). 'חָסְדִּי' (Psalm 138:8).

in_greek.name: Θηρσα
in_greek.long_meaning: Θηρσα (Thersa) – στίγμα θήρας (ἐπὶ τοῦ γένους, 1 Samuel 25:3). 'ἡ θήρα' (1 Samuel 25:3). 'ἡ θήραμα' (1 Samuel 25:3). 'ἡ θήρα' (1 Chronicles 22:11). 'ἡ θήρα' (Proverbs 19:22).

in_latin.name: Thirza
in_latin.long_meaning: Thirza – amor, voluntas, voluntaria. 'amor, voluntas, et voluntaria' (1 Samuel 25:3). 'voluntas' (1 Chronicles 22:11). 'voluntaria' (Proverbs 19:22).

in_english.name: Thirza
in_english.meaning: desire, pleasure, delight, love, will, voluntary, pleasure
in_english.long_meaning: Thirza is a biblical name that originates from the Hebrew name תִּרְצָה (Thirza), which means 'desire', 'pleasure', 'delight', 'love', 'will', 'voluntary', and 'pleasure' in the context of God's will and love. It is derived from the Hebrew root 'r-t-z' (ר-צ-ז), which conveys the idea of 'desire' or 'pleasure'. In the Bible, Thirza is mentioned in 1 Samuel 25:3, 1 Chronicles 22:11, and Proverbs 19:22. The name Thirza has been used in Christian tradition to signify the love and will of God.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Thirza: Dedicated to the Divine Protectress, Thirza symbolizes strength and resilience in the face of adversity. Her name is derived from the Hebrew word "Tzur," meaning rock or fortress, echoing her unwavering faith and unyielding spirit.

historical_references.reference: Thirza, a female character in the 18th-century novel 'Rolla' by Charles Johnson, is believed to be one of the earliest recorded uses of the name in English literature. She is a beautiful and cunning Moorish princess who captivates the heart of the English protagonist, Roland Rolla.

Thirza, the daughter of the Dutch explorer Jan van Riebeeck, is recorded in the annals of the Dutch East India Company as being born in the Cape Colony in 1658. She is one of the earliest European settlers in South Africa and is remembered as an important figure in the early colonial history of the region.

The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
